records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
もしや汝らは
『覇者の証』を探しておる者か？
records.current_English: Do you seek the Proof of Conquest?

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese: 私の思い違いか…
records.current_English: Perhaps I was mistaken...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 『覇者の証』とはいったい…？
records.current_English: What is this Proof of Conquest?

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
…
海を制する者が手にする
とされるもの…
records.current_English:
...They say it passes
 into the hands 
 of the one who rules the seas.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
海を制する者…
興味深い話ですな
records.current_English:
One who rules the seas...
 An intriguing tale.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
我々の目的に少なからず関連が
あるかもしれん。…もう少し詳しく
教えていただけまいか？
records.current_English:
That may have a great deal 
 to do with our own purpose...
 Could you tell us more?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 何かご存じか？
records.current_English: Do you know anything about it?

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
…『証』を探し出す道のりは険しい
生半可な心根の者に話すつもりは
ないが、汝らには、その覚悟があると？
records.current_English:
The road to finding the Proof
 is hard. I tell
 only those truly committed.
 Are you prepared for it?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
海を制する者が持つ、と聞いた以上
それを手に入れるためには
いかなる試練でもいとわぬつもりだ
records.current_English:
If the Proof belongs to whoever
 rules the seas,
 I'll face any trial to claim it.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese: …よかろう
records.current_English: Very well.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
私が知っておるのは、証の地図は
２つの『地図の鍵』を合わせて
初めて役に立つ、ということ
records.current_English:
All I know is that the 
 map to the Proof is useless until
 you bring two Map Keys together.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
それぞれの鍵は、そのままでは
何の意味も持たぬ
records.current_English: Each key alone means nothing.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
すでに気付いておるかもしれぬが
地図の鍵は各地の遺跡に隠されている
こともあれば、思わぬ人物が
握っていることもある…
records.current_English:
As you may already have realized,
 Map Keys are sometimes hidden
 in ruins, and sometimes held 
 by people you wouldn't expect...

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese: 汝に、ひと振りの剣を与えよう
records.current_English: Take this sword.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
汝らに課せられた試練を乗り越え
困っている者を助けるがよい
records.current_English:
Overcome the trials before 
 you, and help those in need.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
己の欲に囚われず、富を持たぬ者に
与えよ。争いの元凶を封じ、広く平和を
もたらすがよい
records.current_English:
Do not be ruled by greed. Give 
 to the poor, stop strife at its
 source, and bring peace far
 and wide.

records.speaker: Priest
records.Japanese:
では、汝らに
神のご加護があらんことを
records.current_English: May God protect you.

records.speaker: Guildmaster
records.Japanese:
行きたいならどこへでも行け！
てめえみたいな使いづれえヤツは
こっちからクビにしてやるよ！
records.current_English:
Go wherever the hell you want! 
 You're too much trouble. 
 You're fired!

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese:
上等だ…
勝手にするがいいさ
records.current_English: Fine by me... Do what you like.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
なんだ？？
ケンカでもあったんでしょうか？
records.current_English: What was that? Were they fighting?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
『クビ』と言っていたな…
あの男、用心棒でもしていたのか？
records.current_English:
He said 'fired'... Was that man
 a bodyguard?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: おい、今の男は何者だ？
records.current_English: Who was that man?

records.speaker: Guildmaster
records.Japanese:
ん？　ああ、あいつはケンカしか
できねえヤツさ
言うことを聞かねえからクビにした
それだけのことさ
records.current_English:
Hm? Oh, him. Fighting's all
 he's good for. 
 Wouldn't do as he was told,
 so I fired him. That's all.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …腕は立つのか？
records.current_English: ...Is he any good?

records.speaker: Guildmaster
records.Japanese:
おいおい、あの男に興味があるのかい？
確かにヤツの腕は超一流だ
だが、荷物持ちぐらい素直にやれと
言いたいね
records.current_English:
Don't tell me you're interested
 in him. He's one hell of a fighter,
 I'll give him that. But is carrying
 a few bags really too much to ask?

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
ふむ…用心棒としては完璧でも
人間性に問題があるようです
プライドが高すぎるのか
協調性がないのか…
records.current_English:
He might be the perfect bodyguard, 
 but I wonder how he'd get along
 with a crew. Too proud, maybe. 
 Or just bad at working with others.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
人のことを言えるほど、シャルルに
協調性があるとは思わんが
…行くぞ
records.current_English:
You're one to talk about teamwork, 
 Charles. Come on.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese: え？　提督、本気なんですか！？
records.current_English: You're serious?!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 一度、直接話してみないと気が済まん
records.current_English:
I won't be satisfied till I've 
 spoken to him myself.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.Japanese:
あれが奴ですね
いやー、いい体格だ。目立ちますね
records.current_English:
There he is. Look at the build on
 him. Hard to miss, isn't he?

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese: 何か用か？
records.current_English: Want something?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ずいぶん身体を
鍛えているようだな
records.current_English:
Looks like you keep yourself 
 in good shape.

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese:
見れば分かることだ
それに、あんたには関係ない
records.current_English:
You can see that for yourself. 
 What's it to you?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
…分からんか
俺はおまえを見込んで声を
かけているのだ
そういう態度は損をするぞ
records.current_English:
Don't you get it? I came 
 over because I think 
 you've got potential. That 
 attitude's doing you no favors.

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese: 何だと！？
records.current_English: What?!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
聞けば用心棒をクビになったそうだな
力をもてあましているのだろう
records.current_English:
I heard you lost your
 job as a bodyguard. You've 
 got more strength than you 
 know what to do with.

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese:
俺を雇うつもりか？
あんたこそ何者だ
records.current_English:
You offering me a job? 
 Who are you, anyway?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
では、自己紹介しよう
俺はFI
スウェーデン海軍所属
警備艦隊を率いる提督だ
records.current_English:
Then allow me to introduce myself. 
 I'm FI, an admiral 
 of the Swedish Navy. I command 
 a patrol fleet.

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese:
へえ、提督か…
だが、俺は船乗りになる気はないぜ
records.current_English:
An admiral, huh... 
 I'm not interested in becoming 
 a sailor.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
おまえの眼力はそんなものか
さっきの雇い主より俺のほうが下
と言うわけだな
records.current_English:
Is that all the judgment 
 you've got? You think I'm
 a worse bet than the man who 
 just fired you?

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese:
！
あんたとは初対面だ
ずいぶんせっかちじゃないか
records.current_English: We just met! What's the hurry?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 優柔不断は男が下がるというもんだ
records.current_English:
A man doesn't do himself any favors
 by dithering.

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese: ぐ…
records.current_English: Grr.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
俺ならおまえの力になれる
ついてくる気があるなら
今すぐ決めてくれ
records.current_English:
I can help you. If you want to come
 with me, decide now.

records.speaker: Al Shin
records.Japanese:
分かった
あんたの船に乗せてもらおう
俺はアルだ。よろしく頼む
records.current_English:
All right. I'll sail with you. I'm 
 Al. Good to meet you.

rows: a worse bet than the man who
All right. I'll sail with you. I'm

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
おい、おっさん！！
おっさんだよ、おっさん！！
records.current_English: Hey, old man! Old man! Yeah, you!

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
そう。あんただ、あんた
港で噂を聞いてきたんだが
この船の提督さんだろ？
records.current_English:
Yeah, you. I heard about 
 you down at the port.
 You're the admiral, right?

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
仕事が欲しくてよ
おっさんの船で働かしてくんねえか？
records.current_English:
I'm looking for work. Got a job
 for me on your ship, old man?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
…何とも横柄な態度ですな
無視しておきますか
records.current_English:
What an insolent fellow... 
 Shall we ignore him?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
まあ、待て。俺は
FI・FA
この船の艦長をやっている
records.current_English:
Hold on. I'm this ship's captain.
 FI FA.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
船で働きたいと言ったな？
俺の艦隊に役立たずは必要ない
おまえに何ができるんだ？
records.current_English:
You want to work aboard my ship? 
 I've no use for dead weight
 in my fleet. What can you do?

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
マンマミーヤ！？
そんなこと見りゃあ分かるだろ
オレのウリは強さと美しさだぜ！
records.current_English:
Mamma mia! Isn't it obvious? 
 I'm strong and I'm gorgeous!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
呆れたやつだ。行きましょう
このような男は概して口先だけの
ものです
records.current_English:
Absurd. Let's go.
 Men like this are usually all talk.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
さっきから、うるせえんだよ
オレが話してんのはこっちの
暗いおっさんだ
あんたじゃねえ
records.current_English:
Will you shut up? I'm talking
 to the gloomy old man
 here, not you!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
言わせておけば…！　貴様っ！
その強さとやら、私が試してやる
抜けっ！
records.current_English:
I've heard enough! Let's see how 
 strong you really are. Draw!

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
そいつぁ、ちょうどいいや
来いよ！
records.current_English: Perfect. Come on!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: やめないか！
records.current_English: Stop this!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
ここはお任せください！
ここまで、提督を侮辱されては
引き下がれません！！
records.current_English:
Leave this to me! I can't let him
 insult you like that, Admiral!

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
どうだい、どうだい！
オレ様は強えんだぜ！
records.current_English:
How do you like that? Told 
 you I was strong!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: むう…！
records.current_English: Grr...!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
ほう…。口先だけだと思ったが…
あのゲルハルトを追い込むとは…
records.current_English:
So he isn't all talk...
 He has Gerhard cornered.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese: いただきだぜ、とどめぇぇ！
records.current_English: I've got you now! You're finished!

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: 甘いわっ！
records.current_English: Too easy!

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese: くッ！！
records.current_English: Gah!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
…さすがゲルハルト
といったところか
だが…。あの男、面白い
records.current_English:
That's Gerhard for you. Still... 
 There's something about
 this fellow.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
おいおい、…ウソだろ
初めて負けちまったぜ
records.current_English: No way... I've never lost before.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
世界は広い
貴様くらいの男は世の中に五万といる
…さて、行きましょうか。提督殿
records.current_English:
It's a big world. Plenty of men
 are as good as you.
 Shall we go, Admiral?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: おい、貴様、船に来るか？
records.current_English: Want to join my ship?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: な、何ですと？
records.current_English: Wh-what?!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
まあ、確かに横柄だが、剣の素質は
なかなか。まだ未熟だが
おまえをここまで苦しめた男も
そうはいまい
records.current_English:
He's certainly rude, but he's
 got a gift with a sword. 
 He's still green, and
 look how hard he pushed you.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese: …まあ、確かにそうですが
records.current_English: ...That is true.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
旅とは人を成長させるもの
こいつもきっと変わるだろう
どうだ？
records.current_English:
Travel makes people grow.
 I think he'll change, too. 
 What do you say?

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.Japanese:
まあ、FI殿が
そこまでおっしゃるのであれば…
records.current_English:
Well, if you feel
 that strongly, FI...

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
お、おい。本当にいいのか？
オレはあんたたちに無礼なことを
やっちまったんじゃねえのかい？
records.current_English:
Y-you really mean it? After
 the way I talked to you?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ならば、その分は働いて返してもらおう
records.current_English: Then make up for it with good work.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
…へっ。じゃあ、そうさせてもらうぜ
すまねえな。オレはアンジェロ
アンジェロ・プッチーニだ
records.current_English:
Heh... All right, I'll take you up 
 on that. Thanks. I'm Angelo. 
 Angelo Puccini.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
ところで提督さんよ。交易で儲けたい
なら、こんな地中海なんかで
ちまちまやってちゃダメだぜ
records.current_English:
By the way, Admiral. If you want to
 make money trading, quit scratching
 around in the Mediterranean.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: なぜだ？
records.current_English: Why?

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
ほう…！
おぬし、なかなか分かっておるな！
records.current_English: Oh! You understand trade well!

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
確かにここいらは航路も発達してて
一見おいしいが、すでに大きな勢力が
開発しつくしてて、うまみが少ねえ
records.current_English:
Sure, the trade routes here
 are well established, so it looks
 promising. But the big powers
 have already developed everything. 
 There isn't much profit left.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: …ふむ

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
やっぱ、外に行かねえとな
アフリカや新大陸は、まだまだ発展する
余地がある。ちょっとの投資で
大きな見返りがあるんだ
records.current_English:
You've got to head farther out.
 Africa and the New World still 
 have plenty of room to grow.
 
 A little investment can bring
 a big return.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
しかも、売ってる交易品が珍しいから
ヨーロッパと往復するだけで
簡単に大金が転がり込んでくる
はずさ
records.current_English:
And they've got unusual goods. Just
 hauling them back and forth
 to Europe should bring 
 in a fortune.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
交易にも造詣が深いとはな
…見かけによらんものだ
records.current_English:
You know your trade, too.
 I wouldn't have guessed.

records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.Japanese:
よせよ
船乗りたちの受け売りさ
records.current_English:
Aw, I just picked it up
 from sailors.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
いやいや
確かにこの男の言う通りじゃ
records.current_English: No, no. The man is quite right.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.Japanese:
せっかく船を買って積荷倉庫が
増えても、なかなかシェアを取れぬ
ヨーロッパでは、交易品を一度に
たくさん商うことができんからのう
records.current_English:
More cargo holds won't help much 
 in Europe. It's hard to get
 market share there, and you can't
 trade in bulk without it.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
早速の助言、感謝する
外洋に出てみることにしよう
records.current_English:
Thanks for the tip. Let's see
 what's out on the open sea.

rows: got a gift with a sword.
look how hard he pushed you.

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese: イアン、これを運んでくれ
records.current_English: Ian, take this over, will you?

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: はい
records.current_English: Yes.

records.speaker: Woman
records.Japanese: あの人よ。キレイねえ……
records.current_English: That's him. Isn't he beautiful...?

records.speaker: Man
records.Japanese: あれ、本当に男かよ
records.current_English: Is that really a man?

records.speaker: Woman
records.Japanese: しっ、聞こえるわよ
records.current_English: Shh. He'll hear.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
（またか……、いい加減にしてくれ
　見せ物じゃない…。）
records.current_English:
(Not again... Give it a rest.
 I'm not here to be gawked at...)

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese: イアン、こっちの酒も頼む
records.current_English: Ian, take these drinks over, too.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: …はい
records.current_English: ...Yes.

records.speaker: Woman
records.Japanese:
きゃっ、イアンさんに
運んでもらっちゃった
records.current_English: Oh! Ian brought it over himself!

records.speaker: Man
records.Japanese:
何喜んでんだ
ちぇっ、面白くねえなあ
records.current_English:
What are you so happy about? Ugh.
 This is getting old.

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese:
イアン、おい
これを向こうのテーブルに
records.current_English:
Ian! Take this to that 
 table over there.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: はい
records.current_English: Yes.

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
おい、ねえちゃん
酌してくれよ。へへ
records.current_English:
Hey, sweetheart. 
 Pour me a drink. Heh.

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
ほんとにキレイだよなあ、あんたは
ああん？
records.current_English: A pretty one, aren't you? Huh?

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
本当に男なのかい？
この肌の白さはふつうじゃあないぜ～
へっへっへぇ～
records.current_English:
Are you really a man? With skin
 that fair? Heh heh heh...

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: 触るな！
records.current_English: Don't touch me!

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese: うおっ、いててて！
records.current_English: Ow! That hurts!

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese: こ、この野郎！
records.current_English: You bastard!

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: （しまった！）
records.current_English: (Damn!)

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
てめえ…
客に対して、たいそうな
もてなしじゃあねえか
records.current_English:
You... That's a fine way to treat
 a paying customer!

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: …失礼、…致しました
records.current_English: ...I beg your pardon, sir.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 親父、酒だ
records.current_English: Barkeep, a drink.

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese:
はいはい、ただいま
……イアン、ちょっといいかい
records.current_English:
Yes, yes, coming right up. 
 ...Ian, a word?

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese:
イアン
おまえにはこの商売
合わないんじゃないか
records.current_English:
Ian... I don't think this line 
 of work suits you.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: 親父さん……
records.current_English: Sir...

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese:
もめごとは、たくさんなんだよ
剣なんか使わなくたって
客のあしらいようはあるだろう
records.current_English:
I've had enough trouble. 
 You can deal with a customer 
 without drawing a sword.

records.speaker: Barkeep
records.Japanese: 悪いが、辞めてもらうよ
records.current_English: Sorry, but I have to let you go.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: ……分かりました
records.current_English: ...Understood.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
あの身のこなし……
剣術を学んでいるのか
それもかなりの使い手のようだ
…話をしてみるか
records.current_English:
The way he moved... He's 
 trained with a sword, and he's 
 good. I should talk to him.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
（クビか…。金もないし
　どうしたものか…。）
records.current_English:
(Fired. No money.
 What am I supposed to do now?)

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: （沖に船が見える…。戻りたい。）
records.current_English:
(A ship out at sea... I wish 
 I could go back.)

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
おーおー、ねえちゃん！
今日はよく会うねえ
records.current_English:
Well, well, sweetheart!
 Running into you again already?

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
へへへ
こんなところに１人でいるなんて
運のねえヤツだ。野郎ども！
records.current_English:
Heh heh... All alone out here? Bad 
 luck for you. Boys!

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
逃げられると思うなよ
さっきはよくも恥をかかせてくれたな！
records.current_English:
You're not getting away. 
 You made a fool of me back there!

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
（この人数じゃ……全部は無理か
　…あのリーダーらしい男だけを
　狙う！）
records.current_English:
(There are too many. 
 I can't take them all. 
 I'll go for the one who
 looks like he's in charge!)

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
てめえら、１人相手に何をもたもた
やってやがる！　しっかりしやがれ！
records.current_English:
What's taking you so long? 
 He's one man! Get on with it!

records.speaker: Sailor
records.Japanese:
ひひひ、きれいな顔してなかなか
やるねえ。戦う姿もなかなか
そそるわい
records.current_English:
Heh heh. Pretty face and you can 
 fight, too. Watching you fight 
 is quite a turn-on.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
はあ、はあ…
（やはり、１人では近づくことも…！）
records.current_English:
Hah, hah... (I can't even
 get near him on my own!)

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
だが、そろそろ終わりのようだな…
早いとこ、やっちまいな！
records.current_English:
Looks like you're about done.
 Finish him off!

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese: なっ…、誰だ！
records.current_English: Wh-who are you?!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
大の大人が数を頼んでとは
感心せんな…
records.current_English:
Grown men, and it takes
 the lot of you to fight
 one? Shameful.

records.speaker: Patron
records.Japanese:
うっ、くそっ…
俺は勝てる戦いしかしない主義だ
覚えてやがれ！
records.current_English:
Damn it... I only pick fights
 I can win. You'll pay for this!

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: これでは酒場で女性が騒ぐわけだ
records.current_English:
No wonder the women in the tavern
 were making such a fuss.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
……容姿なんて…
どうだっていいことだ
records.current_English: ...What does it matter how I look?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
まあ、おまえがそう思うのは
勝手だがな
records.current_English: You're free to think so.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
いや、独り言だ。……悪かった
ありがとう
あなたたちのおかげで命拾いをした
records.current_English:
I was talking to myself. Sorry...
 Thank you. You all saved my life.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
礼を言われるほどのことではない
俺から、その剣の腕を見込んで
頼みがある
records.current_English:
No need to thank us. I saw what
 you can do with a sword, and I'd 
 like to ask you a favor.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese: 私にできることなら……
records.current_English: If it's something I can do...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
先ほどの戦い方、すばらしい剣の腕だ
その腕、世界で試してみないか？
records.current_English:
That was fine sword work back
 there. How'd you like to put 
 it to the test out in the world?

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
…？
どういうことですか
records.current_English: ...? What do you mean?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 俺の船に招きたい
records.current_English: I'd like you aboard my ship.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
本気で言っていただいているのですか
それなら
喜んでお受けしますが…
records.current_English:
Do you really mean that? If so, I'd
 gladly accept, but...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
どういう意味だ？
これが冗談とでも思っているのか？
records.current_English:
What do you mean? Does this sound
 like a joke?

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
いえ、あまりにタイミングが
いいので…
records.current_English:
No, it's just... your timing 
 couldn't be better.

records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.Japanese:
私は失業中の航海士です
ぜひ、あなたの船に乗せてください
イアン・ドゥーコフです
records.current_English:
I'm a navigator out of work. I'd 
 be grateful for a place aboard your
 ship. Ian Dukov, at your service.

rows: trained with a sword, and he's
good. I should talk to him.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 久しぶりに、結構飲んだな
records.current_English:
It's been a while since I drank
 this much.

records.speaker: Cristina Erneco
records.Japanese: 私も、かなり飲んだわね。あら…
records.current_English: I've had quite a bit myself. Oh...

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ん、いい音楽だな
records.current_English: Hm. Good music.

records.speaker: Cristina Erneco
records.Japanese:
この曲…
ちょっと失礼するわね…
records.current_English: This song... Excuse me.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: ん

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
＜客１＞
すげえぞ、あの姉ちゃん
records.current_English: Patron 1: That woman's amazing!

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
＜客２＞
ああ、すげえな、きれいだし
踊りもうまいぜ
records.current_English:
Patron 2: Yeah! She's gorgeous,
  and she can really dance!

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese:
＜客１＞＜客２＞
ブラボー、ブラボー、ブラゥボゥー！
records.current_English: Patrons: Bravo! Bravo! Braaavo!

records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.Japanese: パチパチパチパチ！
records.current_English: Clap, clap, clap!

records.speaker: Cristina Erneco
records.Japanese:
つい、踊っちゃった…
この曲、好きなのよね
records.current_English:
I couldn't help myself.
 I love that song.

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 剣術だけの娘かと思ったが…
records.current_English:
I'd figured you were 
 all about sword fighting...

records.speaker: Cristina Erneco
records.Japanese: 意外だった…？
records.current_English: I surprised you, huh?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese:
まあな…、だがいい踊りだった
ミヴォールが惚れ込むわけだ
records.current_English:
A little. You danced beautifully.
 No wonder Mivor's taken with you.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
そこの提督さん
俺の帆船講座を聞く気はあるかい？
records.current_English: Admiral. Want a sailing lesson?

records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.Japanese: 講座？
records.current_English: A lesson?

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
ここんとこ、ヒマでヒマでしょう
がねえんだ
まあ、人助けとでも思ってさ
records.current_English:
I've been bored out of my skull
 lately. You'd be doing me a favor.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: 聞こう
records.current_English: Listen.

records.speaker: Player choice
records.Japanese: いや、いい
records.current_English: No thanks

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
おいおい。あんた、誰に向かって
講釈たれようとしているのか
分かってんのかね？
records.current_English:
Do you know who you're trying
 to lecture?

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: …ですよねえ
records.current_English: ...Right.

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
船のことなら
今さら聞くまでもないのであります
records.current_English:
When it comes to ships,
 we're past needing lessons.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
まあ、しょうがねえか
あんたら、船に詳しそうだしな
もっと素人っぽい客を待つとするか
records.current_English:
Fair enough. You look like you know
 your ships. I'll wait for somebody 
 who looks a little greener.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
うんうん、いい心がけだね
あんた、大物になるよ
records.current_English: That's the spirit! You'll go far.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
さて、帆船ってくらいだから
帆は船の命だな
records.current_English: A sailing ship lives by its sails.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
よし。まずは四角帆と三角帆の
違いについて説明しよう
records.current_English:
Let's start with the difference
 between square sails 
 and lateen sails.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
四角帆は『スクウェアセイル』とも
いって、船の方向に対して横に
張られた帆、横帆の一種だ
records.current_English:
A square sail is rigged
 across the ship. That's why it's 
 a transverse sail.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
横帆だから、帆を縦にすることが
できねえ。つまり順風には強いが
逆風のときには最適な角度にする
ことはできねえってわけさ
records.current_English:
Square sails can't turn lengthwise.
 They do well downwind, 
 but you can't get the best angle 
 in a headwind.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
三角帆、“通”は『ラテンセイル』って
呼ぶが、四角帆とは逆に、縦に張られて
いて船の方向に対して横に
することができねえ
records.current_English:
Old hands call that triangular sail
 a lateen. It runs lengthwise,
 so you can't turn it crosswise 
 like a square sail.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
逆風のときには、ばっちりの角度に
できるが順風の時にはそれほど
スピードが出ねえのはそういうわけ
だな。…ここまではいいかい？
records.current_English:
You can get just the right angle 
 in a headwind, but you won't go
 as fast with the wind behind you.
 With me so far?

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese: 次は、追加で付けられる帆についてだ
records.current_English:
Next, let's look at the extra sails
 you can add.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
上帆は、正しくは『トップセイル』
といって、各マストの上に取り付ける
小さな横帆のことだ
records.current_English:
The proper name
 for the upper sail is topsail. It's
 a small square sail rigged high
 on each mast.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
斜帆は『ステイセイル』、各マストの
前に付ける小さな縦帆だ。三角帆の
前には付けられねえ。縦帆どうしだと
重なっちまうからな
records.current_English:
A staysail is a small fore-and-aft 
 sail set ahead of each mast. 
 You can't put it ahead of a lateen.
 They'd overlap.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
船首帆は、海の男だったら
『スプリットセイル』と呼んでくれ
こいつは、船の舳先に付ける横帆だ
小型の船に取り付けるのはムリだな
records.current_English:
We sailors call the bow sail 
 a spritsail. It's rigged crosswise 
 at the bow, and you can't fit one
 on a small ship.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
船尾帆は、『ジガースパンカー』とも
いう。縦帆だが、小さなマストが１本
増えるようなものだから
大型船にしか付けられねえぜ
records.current_English:
A jigger spanker is a
 fore-and-aft stern sail. Fitting 
 one is like adding a little mast,
 so it only fits on large ships.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
さて、マストが２本以上ある船は
追い風よりも、やや斜めの風のほうが
スピードが出るって知ってたか？
records.current_English:
Did you know a ship
 with two or more masts sails faster
 with the wind off its quarter
 than dead astern?

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese: そこのあんた、なぜだか分かるかい？
records.current_English: How about you? Know why that is?

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.Japanese:
…ふむ。マストが前後に
並んでいるからですな
records.current_English:
Hmm. Because the masts are lined up
 fore and aft, I suppose.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
そうだ。真後ろからの追い風だと
後ろのマストだけが風を受けて
前のほうにあるマストが役に立たねえ
からな
records.current_English:
Right. When the wind comes straight
 from behind, only the rearmost mast
 catches it. The forward masts don't
 do you any good.

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
斜め後ろから風を受けたときが
一番速えってわけさ。無論、帆の角度は
合わせねえといけねえがな
records.current_English:
That's why you're fastest with the 
 wind at an angle from behind.
 You still have to set the sails
 to match, of course.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.Japanese: なるほど！
records.current_English: Got it!

records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.Japanese:
おお、今まであまり
気にしてませんでした！
そういうわけだったのですね！
records.current_English:
Oh! I'd never given it much
 thought. That explains it!

records.speaker: Shipwright
records.Japanese:
付き合ってくれてありがとうよ
さあ、仕事に戻るとするか
records.current_English:
Thanks for hearing me out. Well, 
 back to work.

rows: across the ship. That's why it's
for the upper sail is topsail. It's
a small square sail rigged high
with two or more masts sails faster
with the wind off its quarter

ordinary_display_leads.shown_next_line: look how hard he pushed you.
